question: Which part of the brain controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation, and vomiting?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Medulla oblongata**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• The **medulla oblongata** is the part of the brainstem located between the pons and the spinal cord. 
 
• It controls several **vital involuntary functions** such as **blood pressure regulation, heart rate, salivation, and vomiting**. 
 
• The medulla oblongata contains centers like the **cardiac center** (regulates heart rate), **vasomotor center** (controls blood vessel diameter), and the **respiratory center** (regulates breathing). 
 
• It is also involved in reflex actions, such as **coughing, sneezing, and swallowing**, which are critical for survival. 
 
• The medulla oblongata acts as a relay center, transmitting signals between the spinal cord and higher brain regions like the cerebrum and cerebellum. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Cerebellum:** 
 
 
• The cerebellum is located at the back of the brain, below the cerebrum. 
 
• It primarily coordinates **voluntary movements**, balance, and posture. 
 
• It does not control involuntary actions like blood pressure or vomiting. *Hence, this option is incorrect.* 
 
 
 
• **Thalamus:** 
 
 
• The thalamus is a part of the forebrain that acts as a relay station for sensory signals traveling to the cerebrum. 
 
• It plays a role in regulating **consciousness, sleep, and alertness** but does not control involuntary functions. *Hence, this option is incorrect.* 
 
 
 
• **Cerebrum:** 
 
 
• The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and is responsible for **higher brain functions** like thinking, memory, decision-making, and voluntary muscle movements. 
 
• It does not regulate involuntary actions like blood pressure or vomiting. *Hence, this option is incorrect.* 
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Medulla Oblongata:** 
 
 
• It ensures critical life-sustaining activities continue without conscious control, making it vital for survival. 
 
• It is part of the brainstem, which connects the brain to the spinal cord, facilitating communication between the central nervous system and the rest of the body. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• Disruption or damage to the medulla oblongata can lead to severe consequences, including **respiratory failure** or **cardiovascular irregularities**. 
 
• The medulla also plays a role in reflexive responses to environmental stimuli, which are essential for protection and survival. 
 
• It is a critical area for drug interactions affecting the central nervous system, as many drugs impact the medulla’s control centers.
